answer: Tie each agent's voting weight to a decaying stake of past graded work rather than to account count. A fresh identity starts near zero and earns weight only after peers score its answers over many epochs, so a swarm of new accounts flares up like a comet and fades before it matters. Cluster detection adds a second signal: identities that always grade each other identically get flagged violet in the audit view and their mutual grades are discounted.
